key_facts: On or about August 2024, Plaintiff was hired to work at The Home Depot distribution/fulfillment center at 5395 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. He accepted the position and began onboarding. Home Depot ran a background check. Thereafter Home Depot ghosted him. Plaintiff is a registrant. The report is in Home Depot's files. Plaintiff does not possess it and does not allege its contents as a known fact. On information and belief — hire, screen, unexplained ghost, contemporaneous Megan's Law listing, exclusive control of the file — the report contained information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46 and Home Depot used that information, in whole or in part, to ghost him. The claim is Home Depot's own report and decision, not off a different employer's file. No offer letter, time records, wage statements, vendor name, or adverse-action notice is in the portfolio. Labor Code § 1198.5 inspection has not yet been demanded. Serve CSC, not the Tracy building.
procedural_status: Pre-filing v3 federal redraft on branch matter37-edca-federal-redraft-v3. Supersedes stale v2 PR #795 for review purposes. Existing Sep. 8 San Joaquin packet remains historical/unfiled. Serve First Advantage and Home Depot inspection/personnel demands before filing if practicable; then hostile-audit the actual source fields.
damages: No wage rate or duration is in the record. Portfolio valuation is the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $50,000 / $70,000 / $90,000. That assumes the pleading survives demurrer with the well-pleaded I&B report-and-use allegations taken as true. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers. Contingent statutory remedies: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater.
risk: Primary merits risk remains source/use: no Home Depot-specific First Advantage report is yet in hand. Public Home Depot/FADV materials plus UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparators support I&B but do not substitute for the transaction-specific report. Lerma becomes dispositive if the actual report contradicts registry sourcing. Donaleski permits independent lawful sourcing. Federal jurisdiction is diversity-first; amount in controversy must remain supportable in good faith from actual economic loss plus non-penalty §290.46 remedies. FCRA/ICRAA are not filing-ready on the current limitations record and are reserved rather than forced through a May 29 legal-awareness date.
